subject: literature
passage: In 1893, Arthur Conan Doyle, tired of his famous detective, sent Sherlock Holmes over a waterfall in the story "The Final Problem." Readers were dismayed, yet a new story set after Holmes's apparent death did not appear until 1903. Literary historian Owen Adebayo argues that Doyle brought the detective back at that point mainly because a publisher offered him an unusually large sum of money, not because readers had protested.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Adebayo's argument?

choices.A: Doyle's letters from 1903 say he agreed to revive Holmes only after a magazine offered him a far larger fee.
choices.B: Readers sent Doyle many angry letters in the months after "The Final Problem" first appeared in a magazine.
choices.C: During the years without new Holmes stories, Doyle wrote several historical novels and a number of plays.
choices.D: Doyle wrote in his diary that he returned to Holmes because so many readers had begged him to do so.

explanation.why: Adebayo claims money, not readers' protests, was the main reason Doyle revived Holmes in 1903. The best support would link Doyle's decision directly to a large payment. Letters in which Doyle says he agreed only after a much larger fee was offered make that link.
explanation.A: Correct. Doyle's own words tie his decision to the larger fee, which is exactly the reason Adebayo gives.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Angry letters show that readers protested, which supports the explanation Adebayo rejects rather than his own.
explanation.C: Incorrect. What Doyle wrote in the meantime does not show why he chose to bring Holmes back.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Doyle saying readers' pleas brought him back would weaken Adebayo's argument.
